chapters.title: Measurement of Length and Motion
chapters.subtitle: Units, careful measurement and types of motion

cards.title: Length and its standard unit
cards.content: Length tells us how far apart two points are. The standard SI unit of length is the metre (m). Smaller lengths are commonly measured in centimetres (cm) or millimetres (mm).

cards.title: How to measure length correctly
cards.content: Follow these steps when using a ruler or metre scale:
steps: Place the scale along the object, with the zero mark at one end.
Keep the scale parallel to the length being measured.
Look vertically above the other end and note the reading.
If the zero mark is damaged, start from another clear mark and subtract the starting reading from the final reading.
cards.note: Write the number together with its unit.

cards.title: Avoid parallax error
cards.content: Your eye should be directly above the mark being read. Looking from an angle can make the reading appear different. This is called parallax error.
cards.examTip: Keep your line of sight perpendicular to the scale at the point you are reading.

cards.title: Different kinds of motion

left.heading: Rectilinear motion
left.content: Movement along a straight line. Example: a car moving along a straight road.

right.heading: Circular motion
right.content: Movement along a circular path. Example: the tip of a fan blade while the fan rotates.

cards.note: The path followed by an object helps us describe its motion.

cards.title: Periodic motion
cards.content: A motion that repeats itself after equal intervals of time is called periodic motion.
cards.highlight: Example: the to-and-fro motion of a swing.

cards.title: Quick unit conversions
cards.note: Convert to the same unit before comparing or adding lengths.

cards.title: Check your recall
cards.question: A student reads a ruler while looking at the mark from a slanting angle. What error may occur, and how can it be avoided?
cards.answer: Parallax error may occur. Keep the eye directly above the mark and look perpendicular to the scale.

cards.title: Classify the motion
cards.question: A point on the edge of a rotating bicycle wheel follows what kind of path?
cards.answer: A circular path, so it shows circular motion.

chapters.title: Real Numbers
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Use prime factorisation to understand HCF and LCM. The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says every composite integer has a unique prime factorisation, apart from order.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: For two positive integers, HCF × LCM = product of the numbers. Use prime exponents carefully.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Real Numbers”?
cards.answer: Use prime factorisation to understand HCF and LCM. The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says every composite integer has a unique prime factorisation, apart from order.

chapters.title: Polynomials
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: A polynomial is an algebraic expression in which the powers of the variable are non-negative integers. Its zeroes are the values that make it equal to zero.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: For ax² + bx + c, sum of zeroes = −b/a and product = c/a.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Polynomials”?
cards.answer: A polynomial is an algebraic expression in which the powers of the variable are non-negative integers. Its zeroes are the values that make it equal to zero.

chapters.title: Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: A pair of linear equations represents two straight lines. Their intersection gives the common solution; parallel or coincident lines explain the other cases.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: For a₁x+b₁y+c₁=0 and a₂x+b₂y+c₂=0, compare coefficient ratios to identify unique, no or infinitely many solutions.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Pair of Linear Equations in Two Variables”?
cards.answer: A pair of linear equations represents two straight lines. Their intersection gives the common solution; parallel or coincident lines explain the other cases.

chapters.title: Quadratic Equations
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: A quadratic equation has the form ax²+bx+c=0, where a≠0. Its roots can be found by factorisation, completing the square or the quadratic formula.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: The discriminant D=b²−4ac determines the nature of roots: positive, zero or negative.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Quadratic Equations”?
cards.answer: A quadratic equation has the form ax²+bx+c=0, where a≠0. Its roots can be found by factorisation, completing the square or the quadratic formula.

chapters.title: Arithmetic Progressions
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: An arithmetic progression has a constant common difference between consecutive terms. The nth term and sum depend on the first term and common difference.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Check the common difference before applying formulas; the sum formula uses the number of terms, not the final term.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Arithmetic Progressions”?
cards.answer: An arithmetic progression has a constant common difference between consecutive terms. The nth term and sum depend on the first term and common difference.

chapters.title: Triangles
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Similarity means corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional. Similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Use AA, SAS or SSS similarity criteria. In a right triangle, the Pythagoras theorem links the hypotenuse to the other two sides.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Triangles”?
cards.answer: Similarity means corresponding angles are equal and corresponding sides are proportional. Similar triangles have the same shape but may differ in size.

chapters.title: Coordinate Geometry
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Coordinate geometry connects algebra and geometry using ordered pairs. Distance, section and area formulas help describe points and figures on the plane.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Keep x-coordinates with x and y-coordinates with y; use brackets carefully when subtracting negative values.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Coordinate Geometry”?
cards.answer: Coordinate geometry connects algebra and geometry using ordered pairs. Distance, section and area formulas help describe points and figures on the plane.

chapters.title: Introduction to Trigonometry
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Trigonometric ratios relate an acute angle in a right triangle to its sides: sine, cosine and tangent, with reciprocal ratios cosec, sec and cot.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Memorise opposite/hypotenuse, adjacent/hypotenuse and opposite/adjacent relative to the chosen angle.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Introduction to Trigonometry”?
cards.answer: Trigonometric ratios relate an acute angle in a right triangle to its sides: sine, cosine and tangent, with reciprocal ratios cosec, sec and cot.

chapters.title: Some Applications of Trigonometry
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Heights and distances problems use angles of elevation and depression with right-triangle trigonometry.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Draw and label a right triangle first. Decide which side is opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse before selecting a ratio.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Some Applications of Trigonometry”?
cards.answer: Heights and distances problems use angles of elevation and depression with right-triangle trigonometry.

chapters.title: Circles
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point. The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Tangents from an external point to a circle are equal in length. Distinguish a tangent from a secant.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Circles”?
cards.answer: A tangent touches a circle at exactly one point. The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent.

chapters.title: Areas Related to Circles
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Sector and segment areas are fractions of the full circle based on the central angle. Arc length is the corresponding fraction of circumference.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Check whether the question asks for a sector, segment, ring or shaded region; subtract areas only after identifying the required shape.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Areas Related to Circles”?
cards.answer: Sector and segment areas are fractions of the full circle based on the central angle. Arc length is the corresponding fraction of circumference.

chapters.title: Surface Areas and Volumes
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Mensuration combines surface area and volume formulas for solids such as cylinders, cones, spheres and combinations of solids.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Convert all measurements to the same unit. For a combined solid, add or subtract only the surfaces that are actually exposed.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Surface Areas and Volumes”?
cards.answer: Mensuration combines surface area and volume formulas for solids such as cylinders, cones, spheres and combinations of solids.

chapters.title: Statistics
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Grouped data can be summarised using mean, median and mode. The median depends on cumulative frequency and the median class.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: For grouped median, identify N/2, locate the median class and substitute its lower boundary, cumulative frequency, frequency and class width correctly.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Statistics”?
cards.answer: Grouped data can be summarised using mean, median and mode. The median depends on cumulative frequency and the median class.

chapters.title: Probability
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: For equally likely outcomes, probability is favourable outcomes divided by total possible outcomes. Probability lies between 0 and 1.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Count distinct equally likely outcomes and avoid counting the same outcome twice.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Probability”?
cards.answer: For equally likely outcomes, probability is favourable outcomes divided by total possible outcomes. Probability lies between 0 and 1.

chapters.title: Chemical Reactions and Equations
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: A chemical reaction rearranges atoms to form new substances. A balanced equation has the same number of each type of atom on both sides, obeying conservation of mass.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Identify the reaction type—combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement or redox—and balance by changing coefficients, never subscripts.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Chemical Reactions and Equations”?
cards.answer: A chemical reaction rearranges atoms to form new substances. A balanced equation has the same number of each type of atom on both sides, obeying conservation of mass.

chapters.title: Acids, Bases and Salts
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Acids produce H⁺/H₃O⁺ ions in aqueous solution; bases produce OH⁻ ions. Neutralisation forms salt and water.
cards.highlight: pH < 7 acid; pH = 7 neutral; pH > 7 base

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Use indicators and pH to compare solutions. Strong/weak describes ionisation; concentrated/dilute describes amount per volume.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Acids, Bases and Salts”?
cards.answer: Acids produce H⁺/H₃O⁺ ions in aqueous solution; bases produce OH⁻ ions. Neutralisation forms salt and water.

chapters.title: Metals and Non-metals
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Metals generally lose electrons to form cations; non-metals generally gain or share electrons. Reactivity determines displacement and extraction methods.
cards.highlight: More reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Remember that reactivity series predicts displacement. Ionic compounds conduct when molten or dissolved, not as solids.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Metals and Non-metals”?
cards.answer: Metals generally lose electrons to form cations; non-metals generally gain or share electrons. Reactivity determines displacement and extraction methods.

chapters.title: Carbon and its Compounds
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Carbon forms covalent bonds and long chains because of tetravalency and catenation. Saturated compounds have single bonds; unsaturated compounds contain double or triple bonds.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Know homologous series, functional groups, combustion, oxidation, addition and substitution reactions; draw structural formulas clearly.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Carbon and its Compounds”?
cards.answer: Carbon forms covalent bonds and long chains because of tetravalency and catenation. Saturated compounds have single bonds; unsaturated compounds contain double or triple bonds.

chapters.title: Periodic Classification of Elements
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: The modern periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number. Elements in a group share valence-electron patterns; periods indicate occupied shells.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Across a period, atomic size generally decreases and metallic character decreases; down a group, atomic size generally increases.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Periodic Classification of Elements”?
cards.answer: The modern periodic table arranges elements by increasing atomic number. Elements in a group share valence-electron patterns; periods indicate occupied shells.

chapters.title: Life Processes
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Living organisms maintain themselves through nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion. These processes exchange matter and energy with the environment.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Trace the pathway, organ and function for each process; compare autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition and aerobic and anaerobic respiration.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Life Processes”?
cards.answer: Living organisms maintain themselves through nutrition, respiration, transport and excretion. These processes exchange matter and energy with the environment.

chapters.title: Control and Coordination
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Nervous and hormonal systems coordinate responses. Neurons transmit impulses; hormones act as chemical messengers through target organs.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Reflex actions are rapid and often involve the spinal cord. Plant hormones coordinate growth and tropic responses.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Control and Coordination”?
cards.answer: Nervous and hormonal systems coordinate responses. Neurons transmit impulses; hormones act as chemical messengers through target organs.

chapters.title: How do Organisms Reproduce?
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Reproduction produces new individuals. Asexual reproduction uses one parent; sexual reproduction involves gametes and fertilisation, generating variation.
cards.highlight: Gametes fuse to form a zygote

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Distinguish pollination from fertilisation in plants and identify the roles of testes, ovaries, uterus and placenta in humans.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “How do Organisms Reproduce?”?
cards.answer: Reproduction produces new individuals. Asexual reproduction uses one parent; sexual reproduction involves gametes and fertilisation, generating variation.

chapters.title: Heredity and Evolution
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Heredity passes traits through genes carried on chromosomes. Variations arise through changes and recombination; natural selection can change trait frequencies over generations.
cards.highlight: Genes → inherited traits; variation fuels evolution

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Separate inherited traits from acquired traits. Evolution describes population change over generations, not a ladder of progress.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Heredity and Evolution”?
cards.answer: Heredity passes traits through genes carried on chromosomes. Variations arise through changes and recombination; natural selection can change trait frequencies over generations.

chapters.title: Light: Reflection and Refraction
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Reflection changes the direction of light at a surface; refraction occurs when light changes speed between media. Spherical mirrors and lenses form images.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Use the correct sign convention and draw principal rays. Distinguish real/inverted from virtual/erect images.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Light: Reflection and Refraction”?
cards.answer: Reflection changes the direction of light at a surface; refraction occurs when light changes speed between media. Spherical mirrors and lenses form images.

chapters.title: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: The eye focuses light on the retina. Accommodation changes lens curvature; scattering and refraction explain several atmospheric optical effects.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Myopia is corrected with a concave lens; hypermetropia with a convex lens. Know dispersion, scattering and the blue appearance of the sky.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “The Human Eye and the Colourful World”?
cards.answer: The eye focuses light on the retina. Accommodation changes lens curvature; scattering and refraction explain several atmospheric optical effects.

chapters.title: Electricity
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge. Potential difference drives current; resistance opposes it. Series and parallel combinations behave differently.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Use V=IR and P=VI. In series, current is common; in parallel, potential difference is common.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Electricity”?
cards.answer: Electric current is the rate of flow of charge. Potential difference drives current; resistance opposes it. Series and parallel combinations behave differently.

chapters.title: Magnetic Effects of Electric Current
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: A current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field. Motors convert electrical energy to mechanical energy; electromagnetic induction produces current from changing magnetic flux.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Use Fleming’s left-hand rule for motor force and right-hand rule for induced current. A split-ring commutator reverses coil current each half-turn.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Magnetic Effects of Electric Current”?
cards.answer: A current-carrying conductor produces a magnetic field. Motors convert electrical energy to mechanical energy; electromagnetic induction produces current from changing magnetic flux.

chapters.title: Our Environment
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Ecosystems contain producers, consumers and decomposers. Energy flows through trophic levels while materials are recycled.
cards.highlight: Energy flow is one-way; nutrients cycle

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Only a small fraction of energy passes to the next trophic level; biomagnification increases concentration of persistent pollutants up food chains.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Our Environment”?
cards.answer: Ecosystems contain producers, consumers and decomposers. Energy flows through trophic levels while materials are recycled.

chapters.title: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: The French Revolution popularised citizenship and the nation as a source of sovereignty. Liberalism, cultural movements and political struggles shaped nineteenth-century nationalism.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Connect unification of Germany and Italy with key leaders, events and the role of conservative powers; distinguish nation-state from empire.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “The Rise of Nationalism in Europe”?
cards.answer: The French Revolution popularised citizenship and the nation as a source of sovereignty. Liberalism, cultural movements and political struggles shaped nineteenth-century nationalism.

chapters.title: Nationalism in India
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Indian nationalism grew through anti-colonial movements, mass mobilisation and shared symbols. Gandhi linked local grievances to broader satyagraha campaigns.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Keep the chronology clear: Rowlatt Act, Jallianwala Bagh, Non-Cooperation, Civil Disobedience and Quit India; note participation and limits across groups.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Nationalism in India”?
cards.answer: Indian nationalism grew through anti-colonial movements, mass mobilisation and shared symbols. Gandhi linked local grievances to broader satyagraha campaigns.

chapters.title: The Making of a Global World
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Globalisation has a long history shaped by trade, migration, conquest, labour and capital flows. The nineteenth century connected economies in new ways.

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Use examples such as silk routes, indentured labour, colonial trade and the Great Depression to explain global interdependence.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “The Making of a Global World”?
cards.answer: Globalisation has a long history shaped by trade, migration, conquest, labour and capital flows. The nineteenth century connected economies in new ways.

chapters.title: Print Culture and the Modern World
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Printing transformed the circulation of ideas, literacy, religious debate and political discussion. Print culture developed differently across societies.
cards.highlight: Print expanded access to ideas and debate

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Explain how print affected reform, public debate and nationalism; distinguish manuscript culture from mass print.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Print Culture and the Modern World”?
cards.answer: Printing transformed the circulation of ideas, literacy, religious debate and political discussion. Print culture developed differently across societies.

chapters.title: Resources and Development
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Resources become useful through technology, institutions and human effort. Sustainable development balances present needs with future generations.
cards.highlight: Sustainable use = present needs + future capacity

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Classify resources by origin, exhaustibility, ownership and status; connect resource planning with conservation and land degradation.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Resources and Development”?
cards.answer: Resources become useful through technology, institutions and human effort. Sustainable development balances present needs with future generations.

chapters.title: Forest and Wildlife Resources
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Biodiversity supports ecological balance and livelihoods. Habitat loss, hunting and development pressures threaten species and forest ecosystems.
cards.highlight: In-situ conservation protects species in natural habitats

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Know conservation categories and community-led examples; distinguish endangered, vulnerable and endemic species.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Forest and Wildlife Resources”?
cards.answer: Biodiversity supports ecological balance and livelihoods. Habitat loss, hunting and development pressures threaten species and forest ecosystems.

chapters.title: Water Resources
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Freshwater is limited and unevenly distributed. Multipurpose river projects support irrigation and power but can also cause social and ecological impacts.
cards.highlight: Rainwater harvesting improves local water security

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Compare dams’ benefits and costs; explain rainwater harvesting and watershed management with local examples.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Water Resources”?
cards.answer: Freshwater is limited and unevenly distributed. Multipurpose river projects support irrigation and power but can also cause social and ecological impacts.

chapters.title: Agriculture
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Agriculture depends on climate, soil, technology, labour and markets. Cropping seasons and farming types vary across India.
cards.highlight: Kharif: monsoon · Rabi: winter · Zaid: short summer

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Compare Kharif, Rabi and Zaid crops; link crop requirements to temperature, rainfall and soil.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Agriculture”?
cards.answer: Agriculture depends on climate, soil, technology, labour and markets. Cropping seasons and farming types vary across India.

chapters.title: Minerals and Energy Resources
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Minerals occur in different geological formations and are essential for industry. Energy resources are renewable or non-renewable.
cards.highlight: Conservation reduces depletion and environmental cost

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Connect mineral type to mode of occurrence and conservation; distinguish conventional and non-conventional energy sources.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Minerals and Energy Resources”?
cards.answer: Minerals occur in different geological formations and are essential for industry. Energy resources are renewable or non-renewable.

chapters.title: Manufacturing Industries
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Manufacturing adds value to raw materials and supports employment, trade and economic development. Industrial location depends on several factors.
cards.highlight: Industry location: raw material + power + labour + market + transport

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Explain agglomeration, industrial pollution and control measures; use examples of major industries and their location factors.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Manufacturing Industries”?
cards.answer: Manufacturing adds value to raw materials and supports employment, trade and economic development. Industrial location depends on several factors.

chapters.title: Power Sharing
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Power sharing reduces conflict and strengthens democracy by distributing authority among organs, levels and social groups.
cards.highlight: Power sharing is both prudent and morally desirable

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Compare Belgium’s accommodation with Sri Lanka’s majoritarian policies; identify horizontal and vertical power sharing.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Power Sharing”?
cards.answer: Power sharing reduces conflict and strengthens democracy by distributing authority among organs, levels and social groups.

chapters.title: Federalism
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Federalism divides power between levels of government, with constitutionally protected jurisdictions. India combines a strong Union with state and local governments.
cards.highlight: Union List · State List · Concurrent List

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Remember the three lists and the role of decentralisation, linguistic states and local self-government.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Federalism”?
cards.answer: Federalism divides power between levels of government, with constitutionally protected jurisdictions. India combines a strong Union with state and local governments.

chapters.title: Gender, Religion and Caste
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Social divisions shape political life. Democracy requires equal citizenship and safeguards against discrimination and domination.
cards.highlight: Secular state: no official religion; equal treatment

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Distinguish gender division, communalism and caste inequality; explain when social differences enrich or threaten democracy.

cards.title: Quick self-check
cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Gender, Religion and Caste”?
cards.answer: Social divisions shape political life. Democracy requires equal citizenship and safeguards against discrimination and domination.

chapters.title: Political Parties
chapters.subtitle: Quick recall · key ideas · exam focus

cards.title: Core idea
cards.content: Political parties contest elections, form governments, shape policies and connect citizens with institutions. They are essential to representative democracy.
cards.highlight: Parties organise political competition and accountability

cards.title: Exam focus
cards.content: Know party functions, challenges such as dynastic succession and money power, and reforms to improve internal democracy.

cards.question: What is the key idea to remember from “Outcomes of Democracy”?

cards.content: Development has different goals for different people. Income matters, but health, education, security, freedom and sustainability also matter.
